title: Calling zuutf from C
text: exactly one C file, R headers, define ZUUTF_DEFINE_API_GET including <zuutf.h>. emits static zuutf_api_get(), resolves table caches : C files include <zuutf.h> alone types. header includes <stddef.h> <stdint.h> nothing else: simdutf header R header, compiles C99 C++17 anywhere.
code: #include <R.h> #include <Rinternals.h> #include <R_ext/Rdynload.h>  #define ZUUTF_DEFINE_API_GET #include <zuutf.h>  SEXP mypkg_valid_utf8(SEXP x) {   const zuutf_api *api = zuutf_api_get();   zuutf_result r = api->validate_utf8((const char *) RAW(x), (size_t) XLENGTH(x));   return Rf_ScalarLogical(r.error == ZUUTF_ERR_SUCCESS); }

title: Calling zuutf from C
text: Validation conversion members return zuutf_result. error ZUUTF_ERR_SUCCESS (0) one ZUUTF_ERR_* codes; count number units read written success, 0-based offset first error input units input error, capacity enough ZUUTF_ERR_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL. Members write take capacity output never write past . length members say much allocate: Conversion members expect valid input report first error; replace nothing. replacement U+FFFD, call utf_convert() R. Base64 members take ZUUTF_BASE64_* flags: ZUUTF_BASE64_URL -_ alphabet, ZUUTF_BASE64_NO_PAD encode without =, ZUUTF_BASE64_STRICT RFC 4648 decoding instead forgiving, ZUUTF_BASE64_EITHER decode either alphabet.
code: size_t need = api->utf8_length_from_utf16le(src, n);   /* bytes */ char *out = (char *) R_alloc(need ? need : 1, 1); zuutf_result r = api->utf16le_to_utf8(src, n, out, need); if (r.error != ZUUTF_ERR_SUCCESS) {   Rf_error("invalid UTF-16 at unit %zu", r.count + 1); }

what: Fast Unicode Validation and Transcoding with simdutf
title: Fast Unicode Validation and Transcoding with simdutf
text: Every Unicode encoding R meets, validated converted memory speed, exact position first error. zuutf validates text converts UTF-8, UTF-16 (LE ), UTF-32 (LE ) Latin-1, counts characters, detects encodings, encodes decodes Base64. bundled copy simdutf, picks SIMD code running processor first use. packages can call functions C registered table. zuutf development. Nothing exported yet; plan first release .agents/roadmap.md.

title: Encode and decode Base64 — base64_encode
text: base64_encode() writes bytes Base64 text; base64_decode() reads back.

title: Encode and decode Base64 — base64_encode
code: base64_encode(x, url = FALSE, pad = TRUE, line_length = NULL)  base64_decode(x, url = FALSE, forgiving = TRUE)

title: Encode and decode Base64 — base64_encode
text: x base64_encode(), raw vector, single string, encoded UTF-8 bytes. base64_decode(), single string raw vector holding Base64 text. url alphabet: FALSE (default) standard one + /, TRUE URL- filename-safe one - _. base64_decode() also takes NA, accepts either. pad Whether base64_encode() writes = padding. line_length NULL (default) one line, positive whole number: line feed ("\n") written every line_length characters, MIME PEM 76 64. CRLF MIME, use gsub() result. forgiving TRUE (default) WHATWG forgiving decoding, FALSE strict RFC 4648; see Details.

title: Encode and decode Base64 — base64_encode
text: base64_encode(): single string. base64_decode(): raw vector. Input chosen mode rejects raises zuutf_base64_error whose offset 1-based position offending character.

title: Encode and decode Base64 — base64_encode
text: Decoding forgiving default, WHATWG "forgiving-base64 decode" : ASCII whitespace (space, tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return) skipped, padding optional, final quantum single character error. forgiving = FALSE reads RFC 4648 section 3.3 strictly: padding required, unused bits last character must zero, whitespace error .

title: Encode and decode Base64 — base64_encode
code: base64_encode(charToRaw("hello")) #> [1] "aGVsbG8=" base64_encode("hello", pad = FALSE) #> [1] "aGVsbG8" base64_encode(as.raw(c(0xfb, 0xff)), url = TRUE) #> [1] "-_8=" base64_encode(as.raw(0:59), line_length = 64) #> [1] "AAECAwQFBgcICQoLDA0ODxAREhMUFRYXGBkaGxwdHh8gISIjJCUmJygpKissLS4v\nMDEyMzQ1Njc4OTo7"  rawToChar(base64_decode("aGVsbG8=")) #> [1] "hello" base64_decode(" aGVs bG8 ")              # whitespace is skipped #> [1] 68 65 6c 6c 6f base64_decode("-_8", url = TRUE) #> [1] fb ff base64_decode("+/8", url = NA)           # either alphabet #> [1] fb ff tryCatch(   base64_decode("aGVsbG8", forgiving = FALSE),   # padding is required   zuutf_base64_error = function(e) e$offset ) #> [1] 7

Matched without regard case hyphens. target encoding: "UTF-8", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32LE", "UTF-32BE" "Latin-1". invalid "error", "replace" "na"; see Details.

title: Convert between Unicode encodings — utf_convert
text: Every pair UTF-8, UTF-16 UTF-32 (either byte order) Latin-1 converts directions. leading byte-order mark matches dropped, "UTF-16", "UTF-32" "auto" chooses encoding; output never carries one. invalid says happens input ill-formed , , "Latin-1" target, code points U+00FF: "error" raises zuutf_encoding_error element's index, offset problem input's code units encoding lies . "replace" writes U+FFFD (? Latin-1, U+FFFD) place maximal ill-formed subpart, WHATWG decoder : one per unpaired surrogate UTF-16, one per --range unit UTF-32, one per partial unit end, one per unrepresentable code point. "na" gives NA (NULL list raw vectors) element. R strings hold U+0000, utf_decode() raises zuutf_nul_error index offset whatever invalid says; utf_convert() keeps .

title: Convert between Unicode encodings — utf_convert
code: # UTF-16 from a Windows tool, with its byte-order mark b <- as.raw(c(0xff, 0xfe, 0x63, 0x00, 0x61, 0x00, 0x66, 0x00, 0xe9, 0x00)) utf_decode(b)                          # "auto" reads the BOM #> [1] "café" utf_decode(b, "UTF-16LE") #> [1] "café"  utf_encode("caf\u00e9", "UTF-16BE") #> [1] 00 63 00 61 00 66 00 e9 utf_convert(charToRaw("caf\u00e9"), "UTF-8", "Latin-1") #> [1] 63 61 66 e9  # ill-formed input bad <- as.raw(c(0x61, 0xff, 0x62)) utf_decode(bad, "UTF-8", invalid = "replace") #> [1] "a�b" utf_decode(bad, "UTF-8", invalid = "na") #> [1] NA tryCatch(   utf_decode(bad, "UTF-8"),   zuutf_encoding_error = function(e) e$offset ) #> [1] 2 utf_encode("\u4e2d", "Latin-1", invalid = "replace") #> [1] 3f

title: Count code points and conversion lengths — utf_count
code: utf_count(c("abc", "caf\u00e9", "\U0001f600", NA)) #> [1]  3  4  1 NA utf_count(as.raw(c(0x3d, 0xd8, 0x00, 0xde)), "UTF-16LE")   # one emoji #> [1] 1  utf_length_as("caf\u00e9", to = "UTF-16LE")   # 8 bytes #> [1] 8 utf_length_as("\U0001f600", to = "UTF-16LE")  # a surrogate pair: 4 bytes #> [1] 4 utf_length_as(as.raw(c(0x63, 0xe9)), from = "Latin-1", to = "UTF-8") #> [1] 3

text: utf_valid() utf_is_ascii(): logical vector, one value per element. utf_error_at(): integer vector 1-based offsets first error, input's code units (bytes UTF-8, Latin-1 ASCII; 16-bit units UTF-16; 32-bit units UTF-32), counted byte-order mark, NA element valid. character vector list keeps names.

title: Validate text in a Unicode encoding — utf_valid
text: Well-formed means Unicode says: UTF-8, overlong forms, encoded surrogates (U+D800 U+DFFF), nothing U+10FFFF truncated sequence; UTF-16, unpaired surrogate; UTF-32, surrogate nothing U+10FFFF. UTF-16 UTF-32 input whose length whole number code units ill-formed last, partial unit. Every byte string valid Latin-1. leading byte-order mark matches encoding skipped. "UTF-16" "UTF-32", byte-order mark chooses byte order, without one input big-endian.

title: Validate text in a Unicode encoding — utf_valid
code: utf_valid(c("abc", "caf\u00e9", NA)) #> [1] TRUE TRUE   NA utf_valid(as.raw(c(0xc3, 0x28)))            # a truncated sequence #> [1] FALSE utf_error_at(as.raw(c(0x61, 0x62, 0xff)))   # third byte #> [1] 3  # UTF-16 with and without a byte-order mark le <- as.raw(c(0xff, 0xfe, 0x61, 0x00, 0x00, 0xd8)) utf_valid(le, "UTF-16")                     # the BOM says little-endian #> [1] FALSE utf_error_at(le, "UTF-16LE")                # unpaired surrogate, unit 2 #> [1] 2  # several byte strings at once utf_valid(list(charToRaw("ok"), as.raw(0xc0), NULL)) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA  utf_is_ascii(c("abc", "caf\u00e9")) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE

title: Information about the bundled simdutf library — zuutf_info

title: zuutf 0.0.0.9000
text: Bundles simdutf 9.2.1, unmodified, every kernel offers scalar fallback kernel every platform. zuutf_info() reports simdutf version, kernel use kernels compiled . utf_valid(), utf_error_at() utf_is_ascii() validate character, raw list--raw input UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32 (either byte order, chosen byte-order mark), Latin-1 ASCII, give offset first error input’s code units. utf_count() counts code points utf_length_as() gives bytes conversion produce. Errors classed conditions zuutf_error (?zuutf_error). utf_convert(), utf_decode() utf_encode() convert every pair UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32 (either byte order) Latin-1, byte-order mark read input never written. Ill-formed input raises error, replaced U+FFFD WHATWG decoder (? Latin-1), gives NA, invalid says. utf_detect() lists encodings bytes , byte-order mark first; utf_decode() uses default. base64_encode() base64_decode() cover standard URL alphabets (either decode url = NA), padding , line wrapping, forgiving (WHATWG) strict (RFC 4648) decoding. registered C table, zuutf_api_v1, installed header zuutf.h, gives packages validation, conversion Base64 C code (vignette("linking")).
